qualitative_transfer_notes: Using a robust level baseline may have limited the influence of a volatile ending observation, but a flat forecast could not track the actual series' changing direction. This is an unverified hypothesis, not an established cause.
The missing target definition, units, dates, and covariates may have made a directional forecast unjustified. This is an unverified hypothesis, not an established cause.
Consider a robust level baseline when the visible history is short and volatile, the target and units are unknown, and no prediction-time evidence supports a direction or trend.
Treat dated text as indirect context unless its relevance to the target is established from prediction-time evidence.
Keep uncertainty explicit when the history is sparse and its dates, units, or relationship to available text are unclear.
Do not apply this lesson when prediction-time evidence establishes a relevant trend, seasonal pattern, or relationship between text and target.
Do not treat a flat forecast as suitable when the task context or visible history supports a different forecasting structure.
Do not treat this single case as proof that a robust level baseline will generalize.

Post-hoc case-local empirical update: The first B forecast imposed a declining path and materially underpredicted the validation window. A short irregular history does not support that continued decay. Avoid mechanically reverting toward older low values after a recent level shift; prefer a stable central level unless the visible pre-target evidence establishes a sustained trend. Do not attempt to predict the timing of isolated excursions.
